document.title: Scenesetter for Your Visit to Islamabad: Afghan Angle
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] Ambassador Simons briefs Assistant Secretary Raphel before her visit. The Taliban are revered in Kandahar but seen as occupiers in Herat and Kabul. Pakistani aid pushes Iran, and probably Russia and India, to back Masoud and Rabbani. US interests include peace, counterterrorism (expel Bin Ladin), narcotics, humanitarian issues and pipelines.

persons.name: John Holzman
persons.role: US Deputy Chief of Mission, Islamabad; made three trips to Afghanistan

mentions.quote: CLASSIFIED BY DCM JOHN HOLZMAN REASON 1.5 (D).
CONSISTS MOSTLY OF JOHN HOLZMAN'S IMPRESSIONS BASED ON HIS THREE TRIPS TO AFGHANISTAN
MULLAH OMAR HAS TRIED TO CREATE A KINDER, GENTLER TALIBAN OCCUPATION, WARNING HIS SOLDIERS THAT THEY WOULD BE BEATEN

events.description: UN working group of second-tier faction leaders met two days in Islamabad; agreed to refer limited prisoner exchange back to leaders; Taliban refused Ramazan cease-fire
US Embassy cable scenesetter for A/S Raphel visit
U.S. Embassy Islamabad sends scenesetter cable on Afghanistan to Assistant Secretary Raphel ahead of her visit.
Taliban battles with Masood since September cost him equipment, territory and taxing power.
UN working group of second-tier faction leaders met for two days in Islamabad; Taliban refused a Ramazan cease-fire but pursued a prisoner exchange.
Mullah Omar warned Taliban soldiers they would be beaten if they beat citizens for not conforming to Taliban mores.

sources_cited: Embassy Islamabad reporting; Holzman's three trips to Afghanistan
key_claims: Taliban rule is accepted in Kandahar but seen as harsh occupation in Kabul and Herat.
Taliban leaders increasingly resent the UN, NGOs and the West.
Radical Islamic governments and organizations are approaching the Taliban; Usama bin Ladin enjoys Taliban hospitality.
Pakistani military aid is judged less significant than rumored, but political, diplomatic and trade support is major.
Masood is much reduced after Taliban battles since September.
Masood and Dostam receive aid from Iran and probably Russia and India.
